prompt:
Feature: subscribe to the household meal plan as an iCal calendar feed.

People plan meals in Mealie but live in their calendar app (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Thunderbird, Outlook). They want to add the household's plan to that app by URL so planned meals show up there and stay current. Calendar apps poll a URL without logging in, so the feed has to be public but guarded by a secret token that a household manager can turn on, replace and turn off.

Expected:

1. Feed token management, for logged-in users and always about their own household, at /api/households/mealplans/ical:
   - GET answers 200 with a JSON object whose mealplanIcalToken is the household's current token, or null when the feed is off (it may also carry householdId). The feed is off by default, for new and existing households. Any member of the household may read the token, including a user without can_manage_household.
   - POST answers 200 (not 201). It turns the feed on with a new random, URL-safe secret token and returns the same object with that token (a non-empty string). Calling it again replaces the token with a different one, and the old token stops working at once.
   - DELETE answers 200. It turns the feed off and returns the object with mealplanIcalToken null; the previous token stops working.
   - POST and DELETE need the can_manage_household permission. A user without it gets 403 and the current token keeps working.
   - The token belongs to the household and must be unique. Storing it is a database change, so add a new Alembic migration revising the current head f3a8b6c1d2e4 (no test depends on the new revision id). The existing migration tests (tests/unit_tests/test_alembic.py and tests/unit_tests/services_tests/backup_v2_tests/test_alchemy_exporter.py) expect the migration files, sorted by file name, to form one chain that ends at the head, so the new file must sort last; the project's date-based file name template does that for a create date after 2026-10-14.
   - The token is a secret. It must not appear anywhere in the responses of GET /api/households/self or GET /api/households/preferences. Updating preferences with PUT /api/households/preferences (a full preferences body, for example the defaults with firstDayOfWeek 1) still answers 200 and leaves the token, and the feed, working.
   - The existing meal plan routes and GET /openapi.json keep working.

2. The feed: GET /api/households/mealplans/ical/{token}, with no authentication at all (no header, no cookie).
   - A token that matches no household (for example a random 32-character string), a replaced token, or the token of a feed that was turned off answers 404.
   - A valid token answers 200 with a Content-Type of text/calendar (a charset parameter is fine) and an RFC 5545 calendar of that household's meal plan entries only. Entries of other households, whether in the same group or another group, never appear.
   - Optional query parameters, camelCase like the rest of the API:
     - types: a meal type to include, repeatable (types=dinner&types=lunch). Values are the PlanEntryType values breakfast, lunch, dinner, side, snack, drink and dessert. Missing or empty means every type. An unknown value such as brunch answers 422.
     - includeNotes: a boolean, default true. With false, entries without a recipe (notes, which only have a title) are left out.
     - tz: an IANA time zone name such as Europe/Berlin, used for timed events. It defaults to the server's local time zone. An unknown zone such as Not/AZone answers 422.
     - A start time for each meal type, in a parameter named after the type: breakfast, lunch, dinner, side, snack, drink and dessert, each a time of day such as 18:30. Entries of a type that has a start time become timed events of one hour, starting at that time on the entry's date in tz. Entries of the other types are all-day events.
   - History: entries dated more than FEED_HISTORY_DAYS (90) days before today, where today is the current UTC date, are left out. The boundary is inclusive: an entry dated exactly 90 days ago is in the feed, one dated 91 days ago is not. Entries for today and later are always in the feed.

3. Feed format. Every line ends with CRLF, the last one included.
   - The body starts with the line BEGIN:VCALENDAR and ends with the line END:VCALENDAR (then CRLF). It carries the usual calendar properties: VERSION:2.0 and a PRODID, and may add CALSCALE:GREGORIAN, METHOD:PUBLISH and an X-WR-CALNAME naming the household.
   - One event per included entry, from a BEGIN:VEVENT line to an END:VEVENT line, with:
     - a UID that is unique and stable for the entry, and a DTSTAMP in UTC (YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ).
     - For an all-day event, the line DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD (the entry's date) directly followed by the line DTEND;VALUE=DATE:YYYYMMDD with the next day's date.
     - For a timed event, the line DTSTART:YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ directly followed by DTEND:YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ one hour later, both converted to UTC. Example: a dinner entry on July 1 with dinner=18:30 and tz=Europe/Berlin (UTC+2 in July) gives DTSTART:<year>0701T163000Z then DTEND:<year>0701T173000Z, while a breakfast entry the same day with no breakfast time stays DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:<year>0701.
     - SUMMARY:<Type>: <title>. <Type> is the meal type's name with its first letter in upper case: in English Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner, Side, Snack, Drink, Dessert (the backend's existing mealplan.entry-type.<type> translations hold these names). <title> is the recipe's name when the entry has a recipe, otherwise the entry's title. The whole value is escaped as an RFC 5545 TEXT value (rules in 4). So a dinner entry for the recipe "Pasta" gives the line SUMMARY:Dinner: Pasta, and a lunch note titled "Leftovers, again; sorry" gives the line SUMMARY:Lunch: Leftovers\, again\; sorry
     - For an entry with a recipe, URL:<BASE_URL>/g/<group slug>/r/<recipe slug>, where BASE_URL is the app setting (the recipe page link the app already puts in its event notifications), not escaped.
     - Optionally a DESCRIPTION (escaped) with the entry's text and the recipe link.
   - Long lines are folded as RFC 5545 asks: every physical line (the body split on CRLF) is at most 75 octets in UTF-8, and each continuation line starts with a single space. Removing every CRLF followed by a space gives back the unfolded lines above.

4. These live in a new service module importable as mealie.services.household_services.mealplan_ical_service (in the package that already holds HouseholdService):
   - FEED_HISTORY_DAYS, a module-level int equal to 90, used for the history window above.
   - _escape_text(value: str) -> str escapes a TEXT value. Each backslash becomes two backslashes, a semicolon becomes \; and a comma becomes \, and every line break (CRLF, a lone LF or a lone CR) becomes the two characters \n. Colons are left alone. For example a\b;c,d followed by CRLF, then e, LF, f becomes a\\b\;c\,d\ne\nf.
   - _fold(line: str) -> str folds one content line, given without its line ending, and returns it without a trailing CRLF. A line of at most 75 UTF-8 octets comes back unchanged (for example SUMMARY:Dinner). A longer line comes back as pieces joined by CRLF plus a single space, where each piece, counting the leading space of the continuation pieces, is at most 75 octets. Breaks fall only between characters, never inside a multi-byte character such as an emoji or ä, and removing every CRLF plus space gives the original line back.

No new third-party package is needed. The upstream change also adds a meal planner dialog for the feed; UI changes are not part of this task.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests tests/unit_tests/services_tests tests/unit_tests/test_alembic.py` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
